headline: A stock rebound and profit-taking lift long CGB yields late; the 5Y hits a new low on ample cash
summary: CGBs split on Wednesday. Futures closed slightly higher, but cash long bonds were sold after the futures close as stocks rebounded: the CCDC 10-year rose 0.9bp to 1.635% and the 30-year 0.8bp to 2.049%. The front end and belly kept rallying on another RMB1tn of overnight cash, with the 5-year down 0.8bp to 1.341% (a new low) and the 2-year down 0.7bp to 1.233%, so 2s10s steepened 1.6bp to 40.2bp. Policy banks moved with CGBs: CDB 10-year at 1.670% is still 3.5bp over, ADBC and EXIM about 6bp and 5.5bp.
drivers: The Shanghai Composite rose 0.91% to 3,681, Shenzhen 2.02% and ChiNext 3.4% as tech stocks recovered with Asia, on turnover of about RMB1.64tn. With the 10-year and 30-year at 1-year lows, traders cashed in long bonds after futures settled, so TL's 0.04% gain did not stop the 30-year rising 0.8bp.

The PBOC lent another RMB1tn overnight plus RMB151bn of 7-day repos at 1.40%, a RMB151bn net injection over month-end tax and bond payments. Overnight Shibor held at 1.281% and 7-day Shibor fell 0.8bp to 1.34%, which kept short and 5-year yields falling.

Huatai and GF Securities both warn that the payoff for adding duration is thin at these levels and that regulators have already given some institutions window guidance on bond buying. That caps the long end until the overnight policy rate is set on Nov 2.
ADBC sold 3-year and 10-year bonds at 1.232% and 1.634%, the 10-year with 8.1 times cover, and EXIM placed short floaters. Solid demand let policy banks keep pace with CGBs, so spreads barely moved.
data: A beat driven by AI hardware, metals and oil-linked prices, not households; bonds looked through it.
RMB700bn 1Y vs RMB900bn maturing (net −200bn); outright reverse repos +400bn net in Oct
A tidy-up, not tightening: medium-term liquidity is still up RMB200bn in October, and the overnight rate is now the policy signal.
Firmer growth, near the bottom of the 4.5–5% target. It eases pressure for stimulus but was not strong enough to sell bonds.
Growth is led by exports and AI-linked output, with households and property still weak. It does not challenge low yields.
CPI 0.9% (f 1.0%), core 1.0%; PPI 5.0% (f 4.4–4.5%), highest since Jun 2022
Cost-push from oil and AI components, not demand. Bonds ignore it unless core CPI follows.
New loans RMB1.08tn (f 0.98tn); TSF 3.55tn; M2 7.2% (f 7.4%); M1 3.2%
Loan growth is at a record-low 4.8% and money growth is slowing. Weak credit demand keeps banks buying bonds.
As expected. The policy signal now comes from the overnight-rate switch, not the LPR.
view: Mildly bullish, with the long end pausing, for the next 1–2 weeks. I keep the expected CCDC 10-year range at 1.59–1.66%. Overnight cash at the 1tn cap and a likely overnight policy rate near 1.25% on Nov 2 favour the front end and the 10-year, but a stock rebound, crowded positioning and regulators' attention limit the 30-year, so I prefer 10-year duration and stay underweight the rich 5–7Y belly and policy banks against CGBs. A 1.25% or lower overnight rate or a soft October PMI would take the 10-year toward 1.60%; a sustained equity rally or a pro-growth plenum message would push it back to 1.65–1.66%.

buckets.name: CGB 1–2Y
buckets.why: The 2-year fell 0.7bp to 1.233%, in the 4th percentile of its year (average 1.313%), and the 1-year at 1.169% is now about 11bp below overnight Shibor (1.281%). The front end already prices an overnight policy rate near 1.25%.
buckets.call: Hold; don't chase below 1.20% on the 2-year. Add only if the overnight rate is set below 1.25%.

buckets.name: CGB 5–7Y belly
buckets.why: The 2s5s10s fly fell to −18.6bp, a 1-year low (0th percentile, average −7.4bp), as the 5-year set another low at 1.341%. The 5s10s flattener from ~29bp is open and slightly offside: 5s10s steepened 1.7bp to 29.4bp (84th percentile, average 26.3bp), still inside the 31bp stop.
buckets.call: Keep the 5Y-into-10Y switch (5s10s flattener) from ~29bp, target 25bp, stop 31bp.

buckets.name: CGB 10Y
buckets.why: The 10-year rose 0.9bp to 1.635%, still in the 1st percentile of its year, but against its neighbours it is cheap: the 7s10s20s fly is −22.0bp, in the 95th percentile against a −29.3bp average. It remains the best value on the curve for duration.
buckets.call: Range 1.59–1.66%. Buy on a back-up to 1.65–1.66%; take profit near 1.61%.

buckets.name: CGB 30Y
buckets.why: 10s30s was flat at 41.4bp, in the 22nd percentile and below its 45.4bp average, and the 30-year rose 0.8bp to 2.049% on late profit-taking. Weak domestic demand supports it, but the long end is the most crowded trade and the first to give back when stocks rally.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add above 2.10% (10s30s ~46bp); poor risk/reward below 2.05%.

buckets.name: Policy banks 2–10Y vs CGB
buckets.why: CDB 10-year is 3.5bp over CGB, in the 3rd percentile against a 10.1bp average, and CDB 2-year and 5-year spreads (12.4bp and 10.4bp) sit in the 2nd and 6th percentiles. The switch from ~3bp is open and flat today; policy financing tools still need funding.
buckets.call: Keep the CDB 10Y into CGB 10Y switch from ~3bp, target 8bp, stop 1bp.

buckets.name: ADBC/EXIM vs CDB 10Y
buckets.why: ADBC 10-year yields 2.7bp more than CDB, in the 71st percentile against a 1.2bp average; EXIM is 1.75bp over, near its 2.0bp average. Today's ADBC 10-year drew 8.1 times cover, so the pickup is about supply, not credit.
buckets.call: Hold ADBC/EXIM 10Y rather than CDB 10Y for the ~2–3bp pickup.

buckets.name: Policy banks 20–30Y
buckets.why: CDB 20-year is 6.4bp over CGB, in the 8th percentile against a 10.8bp average, and the 30-year spread is 11.0bp, the bottom of its 11.0–16.9bp range (average 12.8bp). Policy bank long bonds simply track CGBs, so there is no spread cushion left.
buckets.call: Prefer CGB 20–30Y to CDB 20–30Y; revisit policy bank long bonds above a 13bp 30-year spread.

cgb:1.note: Down 1.1bp to 1.169%, about 11bp below overnight Shibor (1.281%).

cgb:2.note: Down 0.7bp to 1.233%, pricing a ~1.25% overnight policy rate.

cgb:5.note: Down 0.8bp to 1.341%, another 1-year low; still the richest point on the curve.

cgb:7.note: Up 0.1bp to 1.447%, just off its 1-year low.

cgb:10.note: Up 0.9bp to 1.635% on late profit-taking, after Tuesday's 1.626% low.

cgb:30.note: Up 0.8bp to 2.049% as stocks rebounded, though TL futures closed up 0.04%.

cdb:2.note: Down 0.2bp to 1.357%, about 12bp over CGB, near the 1-year tight.

cdb:10.note: Up 0.9bp to 1.670%, about 3.5bp over CGB, near its 1-year tight.

cdb:30.note: Up 0.8bp to 2.159%, tracking CGB; about 11bp over, the 1-year tight.

adbc:10.note: Up 0.7bp to 1.697%, about 6bp over CGB; 10Y auction drew 8.1x cover.

exim:10.note: Up 0.7bp to 1.687%, about 5.5bp over CGB and 2bp over CDB.

watch: Next: the Fed decision (early Oct 29 Beijing), the Fifth Plenum communiqué (Oct 29), October PMIs (Sat Oct 31), the end of the overnight repo series and the overnight policy rate the PBOC sets (Nov 2), Hong Kong accepting CGBs as margin collateral from Nov 2, then October trade, inflation and credit data.
